title: The updated version is not available
author: JohnnyB-ro
summary: PowerToys 0.100.2 rejects the four-component latest release tag, so the update check reports no update; current main contains the parser fix but a servicing Store release is still needed.

status.label: Design ready for servicing release
status.detail: The client-side VersionHelper parser is the confirmed failure boundary; approve a backport and release validation plan.

next_action.label: Approve fix design
next_action.reason: The root cause and atomic parser/backport plan have independent adversary sign-off.

judgment.rationale: The reporter's 0.100.2 binary predates the four-part version parser introduced for preview releases. The current stable tag has four numeric components, which the old stream parser leaves unread and rejects via ss.eof().
evidence: The issue reports Store-installed PowerToys 0.100.2 does not find the available 0.101.2362.0 update.
The reporter reproduced the result after removing and reinstalling from the Microsoft Store.
The discussion identifies the old src/common/version/helper.cpp stream parser and its ss.eof() check.
The current release tag is v0.101.2362.0, a four-component version.
Current main contains four-part VersionHelper parsing and native tests, but that does not repair the already-published 0.100.2 binary.
No linked open PR, assignee, duplicate resolution, or fork implementation covers the servicing release for this issue.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve the fork mirror design for a servicing backport and release validation; do not create code or an upstream PR in this workflow.

fix_assessment.rationale: Current main has the parser implementation, but the affected 0.100.2 Store binary still needs a supported servicing package and update-path validation.

proposed_fixes.title: Backport four-component version parsing to the Store servicing release
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The 0.100.2 VersionHelper::fromString implementation parses three integers and requires stream EOF. A four-component release tag leaves the build component unread, so the available release is discarded before comparison.
plan: Backport the four-component VersionHelper data model and strict parser from src/common/version/helper.h and helper.cpp to the servicing baseline.
Preserve three-part compatibility, optional v/V prefixes, accepted preview suffix handling, strict malformed-input rejection, and numeric build ordering.
Add native regression tests for four-part tags, leading zeros, suffixes, invalid inputs, formatting, and comparisons.
Build and publish the matching Store servicing package, then verify that the update path detects and installs a newer release without changing Store identity or channel policy.
verification: Confirm v0.101.2362.0 parses as 0, 101, 2362, 0 and compares newer than the installed 0.100.2 value.
Install the affected 0.100.2 Store package and reproduce the no-update result before the servicing build.
Install the servicing package, press Check for updates, and verify the newer release is detected and completes through the Store.
Run the existing CommonLib native tests and verify legacy three-part and stable-channel behavior.

confidence.rationale: Issue evidence, the maintainer diagnosis, the release format, and the current parser fix align directly; only servicing rollout logistics remain uncertain.

issue_context.summary: A Microsoft Store installation at PowerToys 0.100.2 does not offer the available four-component stable release.
known_information: The reporter uses PowerToys 0.100.2 from the Microsoft Store on Windows NT 10.0.26200.0.
The latest stable release is 0.101.2362.0 and its tag has four numeric components.
The reporter reproduced the issue after reinstalling from the Store and supplied a screenshot of the update result.
The issue discussion identifies the old VersionHelper stream parser and EOF check as the mismatch.
Current main contains a four-part parser and matching native tests introduced by the preview-version work.
inferences: The Store update service is not the primary failure; the client rejects the release metadata before it can offer the update.
A servicing package is needed for users who already have the released 0.100.2 binary.
The parser change should be backported without changing package identity or update-channel selection.
issue_context.analysis: The failure is a deterministic compatibility gap between the shipped three-part parser and the newer four-part release format. The code fix is already validated on current main, but the user-visible repair requires a servicing release and an end-to-end Store check.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue body, all four comments, labels, assignees, and timeline; no linked fix or duplicate resolution was found.
Downloaded and inspected the supplied PNG screenshot; it provides UI corroboration but no additional diagnostic data.
Inspected src/common/version/helper.cpp, helper.h, and UnitTestsVersionHelper.cpp on the local PowerToys clone.
Compared parser history before and after the preview release versioning change and confirmed the old ss.eof() behavior and current four-part implementation.
Inspected the release-tag parse in src/common/updating/updating.cpp and confirmed it depends on VersionHelper::fromString.

design.root_cause: PowerToys 0.100.2's three-component VersionHelper::fromString rejects the four-component stable release tag v0.101.2362.0 because the fourth numeric component remains unread and ss.eof() is false. The updater therefore discards the candidate release and reports no update.
evidence: Issue report: Store-installed 0.100.2 remains installed when checking for updates.
Discussion: old helper.cpp uses if (!ss.fail() && ss.eof()) after reading only major, minor, and revision.
Release state: v0.101.2362.0 is the available four-component stable tag.
Code history: current main replaced the stream parser with bounded three/four-part parsing and added build-aware tests.

affected_files.purpose: Declares the comparable version value and parser API.
Parses release/file versions and formats comparable values.
Reads release metadata and parses tag_name through VersionHelper.
Native regression tests for construction, parsing, comparison, and formatting.
Builds the native CommonLib unit-test binary.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The affected baseline stores only major, minor, and revision.
implementation_steps.change: Add a defaulted build component so existing three-part call sites remain source-compatible while four-part release versions are represented and compared.
edge_cases: Keep build zero as the legacy absent component.
Preserve defaulted constructor behavior and comparison ordering.
tests: Constructor initializes build to zero by default and to the supplied value when present.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The old stream parser reads three integers and requires EOF, rejecting four-part tags.
implementation_steps.change: Parse exactly three or four dot-separated decimal tokens after trimming v/V and a supported preview suffix; reject malformed or extra components; construct the build-aware VersionHelper and preserve three-part formatting for build zero.
implementation_steps.code_block:
+ trim optional v/V and supported suffix
+ size_t parts[4]{};
+ parse each non-empty decimal token until the full string is consumed
+ accept only 3 or 4 tokens
+ return VersionHelper(parts[0], parts[1], parts[2], parts[3])
edge_cases: Reject empty, partial, nonnumeric, extra-part, invalid-suffix, and overflow inputs.
Do not accept arbitrary trailing text.
tests: Four-part stable tag and leading-zero build parse.
Accepted preview suffix parses; malformed suffix rejects.
Three-part parsing and zero/non-zero formatting remain unchanged.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: An unparsable four-part tag is ignored, leaving no newer release candidate.
implementation_steps.change: Consume the corrected VersionHelper result without changing stable-release selection, Store behavior, or existing non-fatal parse-failure handling.
edge_cases: Do not enable preview releases for stable users as a side effect.
tests: Use a four-part stable tag in the update comparison path and assert it is newer than 0.100.2.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Existing tests cover the current four-part implementation on main but not the shipped old baseline's regression behavior.
implementation_steps.change: Retain and, if needed on the servicing branch, add tests for four-part narrow/wide parsing, build comparison, leading zeros, suffix validation, malformed input, and formatting.
edge_cases: Tests must be deterministic and network-free.
Use the existing Microsoft Native CppUnitTestFramework conventions.
tests: Run the existing CommonLib native test binary through Visual Studio Test Explorer or vstest.console.exe.

implementation_steps.file: servicing release pipeline and Store package metadata
symbols: existing release/build entry points for the supported servicing branch
implementation_steps.current_behavior: Users on the published 0.100.2 package cannot receive the parser change already present on current main.
implementation_steps.change: Build and publish a supported servicing package containing the parser fix, preserving package identity and update-channel policy; validate embedded version and release tag before rollout.
implementation_steps.code_block: build servicing package -> verify embedded four-part version -> publish through existing Store/release path -> test Check for updates
edge_cases: Coordinate release numbering and Store propagation.
Do not create an upstream PR in this design-only workflow.
tests: Install 0.100.2 as a reproduction control, then install servicing build and verify detection, update, restart, and reported version.

verify: Use the existing native build workflow for src/common/UnitTests-CommonLib/UnitTests-CommonLib.vcxproj and run tests with Visual Studio Test Explorer or vstest.console.exe; do not use dotnet test.
Before the fix, install Store package 0.100.2, press Check for updates, and observe that v0.101.2362.0 is not offered.
After the servicing build, press Check for updates and verify the newer release is detected, installed through the Store, and reported after restart.
Verify ordinary three-part tags, preview suffix policy, malformed input rejection, stable-channel selection, and build ordering.
risks: A servicing Store release requires release coordination and may be delayed by Store propagation.
Version parsing is shared by update metadata and persisted/file-version comparisons; permissive parsing could create incorrect ordering.
Changing package identity or channel policy while servicing could introduce a separate installation or preview-update regression.
alternatives: Change only Store or release metadata: rejected because the client parser is the direct compatibility failure.
Truncate four-part tags to three components: rejected because it loses build ordering.
Rely only on current main: rejected because already-installed 0.100.2 binaries remain broken.
Force updates outside PowerToys: rejected because the Store works for other applications and the client rejects the release candidate.

adversary.sign_off: No blocking objections after two independent adversary rounds.
non_blocking_notes: The parser fix is already present on current main; the remaining deliverable is a servicing release for the affected Store binary.
Release-channel and Store propagation checks must remain explicit.
